beats.intro: Chapter six, lesson five. Mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes. [[leaf]]A leaf in sunlight looks calm, but every cell inside it is busy. [[map]]Zoom in, and here is the plant cell from our tour. [[lit]]Three kinds of organelle are lit up. [[ask]]Two of them change energy from one form to another. The third deals with a harmful by-product of the cell's chemistry.
beats.mito: Start with the mitochondrion. [[where]]Nearly all eukaryotic cells have them, plants included. [[resp]]A mitochondrion is the site of cellular respiration, a metabolic process that generates {{ATP|A T P}}. [[atp]]ATP, adenosine triphosphate, is the energy carrier the cell spends on its work. [[muscle]]A runner's leg muscle spends a great deal of ATP, so its cells are full of mitochondria. [[plant]]A leaf cell needs ATP too, all day and all night, so it has mitochondria as well.
beats.mstruct: Now open one up. [[two]]A mitochondrion has two membranes. [[outer]]There is an outer membrane. [[inner]]And there is an inner membrane, which folds inward. [[cristae]]The folds are called cristae. [[area]]More folding means more surface, and the enzymes that make {{ATP|A T P}} work on that surface. [[ims]]The gap between the two membranes is the intermembrane space. [[matrix]]Inside the inner membrane is the matrix, where some steps of cellular respiration happen. [[ribo]]The matrix also holds a little DNA, and small ribosomes of its own.
beats.q1: Quick check. Find the part of the mitochondrion that fits the clue.
beats.chloro: Now the chloroplast. [[leaf]]Chloroplasts are found in the leaves and other green parts of plants, and in algae. [[photo]]A chloroplast is the site of photosynthesis. [[plastid]]It is one kind of plastid, a family of organelles that contain pigments. [[chl]]Its pigment is chlorophyll, the green that colors a leaf. Chlorophyll captures light. [[sugar]]Photosynthesis uses that light energy to build sugar from carbon dioxide and water, and it releases oxygen.
beats.cstruct: Open a chloroplast. [[env]]Like a mitochondrion, it has a double membrane, an inner and an outer. [[stroma]]Inside is a fluid called the stroma. [[thy]]In the stroma float thylakoids, flattened sacs made of membrane. [[granum]]Thylakoids are stacked like coins, and one stack is a granum. Many stacks are called grana. [[work]]The chlorophyll, and the enzymes that carry out photosynthesis, are part of this machinery.
beats.twins: These two organelles have a lot in common. [[no]]Neither one belongs to the endomembrane system. They are not part of the chain of membranes that vesicles link together. [[dbl]]Both have a double membrane. [[dna]]Both contain their own DNA, and their own small ribosomes. [[import]]But they do not build everything themselves. Most of their proteins are made on free ribosomes in the cytosol, and then imported. [[swap]]One changes the energy in food into ATP. The other changes the energy in light into sugar.
beats.leafday: Now put them to work in one leaf cell. [[sun]]In sunlight, the chloroplast makes sugar and releases oxygen. [[burn]]In the same cell, a mitochondrion takes that sugar and oxygen. [[make]]Cellular respiration then makes ATP from them. [[note]]So the products of one organelle feed the other. But only the chloroplast captures light.
beats.q2: Quick check. Sort each clue to the right organelle.
beats.perox: The third organelle is the peroxisome. [[one]]It has a single membrane, not two. [[ox]]Peroxisomes carry out oxidation, reactions that use oxygen to break down molecules. [[h2o2]]Some of these reactions make hydrogen peroxide, which is harmful to the cell. [[cat]]The peroxisome holds an enzyme called catalase, which converts it. [[eq]]Two hydrogen peroxide molecules become two water molecules, and one oxygen molecule is released. [[safe]]Because this happens inside the peroxisome, the rest of the cell is shielded.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration and generate ATP. Their inner membrane is folded into cristae, which gives more surface for ATP making. [[w2]]Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis. They hold chlorophyll, in thylakoids stacked into grana, inside the stroma. [[w3]]Both have two membranes, their own DNA and ribosomes, and are not part of the endomembrane system. [[w4]]Peroxisomes have one membrane, and turn hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. [[end]]Now try the practice.
